title.zh: 用“弱信号源”替代“算法新闻源”
title.en: Replacing News Feeds with a Weak-Signal Radar

old_assumption.zh: 保持敏锐的方式是每天刷热搜、科技媒体和公众号推送。
old_assumption.en: Staying sharp means checking tech news, social feeds, and trending topics daily.

new_shift.zh: 媒体报道的永远是已经卷成红海的“滞后共识”；真正的早期变化藏在 GitHub 提交记录、小众论坛吐槽、产品更新日志和论文附录里。
new_shift.en: Media reports lagging consensus; real early shifts hide in GitHub commits, niche forum complaints, changelogs, and paper appendices.

zh: 我想持续追踪 [某个具体领域] 最早期的真实变化，但不想看二手媒体通稿。请帮我列出 5 个高信噪比的一手弱信号来源，以及每周 15 分钟的扫描方法。
把下面这段我刷到的零散观察：[粘贴你的观察或链接]，往上抽象一层：它背后反映的底层结构变化是什么？在哪些相邻领域可能出现类似机会？
en: I want to track early shifts in [Specific Field] without reading secondhand media hype. Give me 5 high-signal primary sources and a 15-minute weekly scanning routine.
Abstract this raw observation up one level: [Paste Observation]. What structural shift does it signal, and what adjacent domains might be affected next?

note.zh: 大量独立开发者与前沿实验项目的最早一手发布阵地
note.en: Primary early-stage launchpad for indie tools and frontier experiments

title.zh: 把 AI 当“红队死对头”而不是“顺从助手”
title.en: Using AI as an Adversarial Red-Teamer, Not a Yes-Man

old_assumption.zh: 遇到决策纠结时，让 AI 帮自己补充论据、优化方案、给点鼓励。
old_assumption.en: When making decisions, people ask AI to polish their plan and validate their reasoning.

new_shift.zh: 大模型默认讨好用户（Sycophancy），它最被低估的用法其实是强制它扮演冷酷的反对派，在投入时间前先做“事前验尸（Pre-mortem）”。
new_shift.en: LLMs default to sycophancy—their most underused superpower is role-playing a ruthless skeptic to run a pre-mortem before you commit months of effort.

zh: 我正打算做这个决定/项目：[描述你的想法]。请收起礼貌和鼓励，扮演最挑剔的行业老兵，给出 5 个最可能导致这件事在 3 个月内彻底失败的致命盲区。
针对我的判断：[填入你的核心观点]，帮我构建一个最强版本的反方论证（Steelman），并指出只需要验证哪 1 个事实就能推翻我现在的假设。
en: I am about to commit to [Your Decision/Project]. Drop all politeness and act as a ruthless domain veteran: give me the 5 sharpest reasons this fails within 3 months.
Build the strongest possible counter-argument (Steelman) against my belief that [Your Belief], and identify the single falsifiable test that would prove me wrong.

signals.name: Gary Klein — Performing a Project Premortem (HBR)

note.zh: 经典决策方法“事前验尸”：假设项目已经失败，倒推最可能的死因
note.en: Classic decision method: assume the project failed and work backward to find hidden flaws

title.zh: 用“结构同构”做跨学科解法移植
title.en: Cross-Domain Solution Transfer via Structural Analogy

old_assumption.zh: 遇到难题时，只在自己所在行业的最佳实践里找答案。
old_assumption.en: When stuck on a hard problem, look only at best practices inside your own industry.

new_shift.zh: 你所在领域卡了十年的难题，往往在另一个毫不相干的学科（如航空、生态学、游戏设计、精益制造）里早就有成熟到烂大街的标准解法。
new_shift.en: A problem your industry has struggled with for a decade is often already a solved textbook pattern in aviation, ecology, game design, or manufacturing.

zh: 我目前卡在一个难题上：[描述你的问题，去掉行业黑话]。请先把这个问题抽象成底层结构，再从 3 个完全不相关的领域（如游戏设计、急诊医学、航空管制、生态学）找出成熟解法并翻译回来。
如果把 [你正在做的项目/习惯] 当作一款电子游戏的机制来重新设计，有哪些“即时反馈、难度曲线、防挫败”的设计可以直接照搬过来？
en: I am stuck on [Describe Problem Without Jargon]. Abstract it to its core mechanics, then transplant proven solutions from 3 unrelated fields (e.g., aviation, game design, ER medicine, ecology).
If you redesigned [Your Project/Habit] using video game design principles, which feedback loops, difficulty curves, and anti-friction mechanics would you steal?

note.zh: 把航空飞行检查单跨界移植到外科手术室，大幅降低事故率
note.en: Transplanting aviation checklists into hospital operating rooms to cut errors dramatically

title.zh: 先花 3 分钟“改写问题”，再让 AI 回答问题
title.en: Reframing the Question for 3 Minutes Before Asking AI for Answers

old_assumption.zh: 脑子里刚冒出一个模糊念头，就直接丢给 AI 要方案，拿到平庸答案再怪 AI 不够聪明。
old_assumption.en: Typing a vague half-baked thought straight into AI and blaming generic answers on the model.

new_shift.zh: 80% 的平庸回答源于模糊提问；先让 AI 帮自己暴露前提假设、拆解隐藏变量、生成 3 个不同切角的精准母题，后续产出质量会呈阶梯式跃升。
new_shift.en: Most generic AI outputs come from vague questions—spending 3 minutes surfacing hidden assumptions and sharper angles upgrades every answer that follows.

zh: 我现在的模糊想法是：[粘贴你的模糊念头]。先不要给我最终方案，请帮我找出这句话里的 3 个隐含前提，并把我的问题改写成 3 个角度完全不同的精准提问。
针对 [你最近卡住的一个难题]，请用“五问法/反事实追问”帮我确认：我真正要解决的核心矛盾到底是什么，还是只是在修枝叶？
en: My rough thought is: [Paste Rough Thought]. Before solving it, surface 3 hidden assumptions in my framing and rewrite this into 3 sharper questions from distinct angles.
For [Problem You're Stuck On], help me test whether I'm solving the real bottleneck or polishing a symptom, and suggest the sharpest question to ask next.

note.zh: 用结构化母题库把“不知道该问什么”变成可复用的探索起点
note.en: Turning 'unknown unknowns' into structured starting questions before deep AI execution

title.zh: 区分“可逆门”与“单向门”，该快的地方别慢
title.en: Separating Two-Way Doors from One-Way Doors to Move Faster

old_assumption.zh: 所有决定都要反复权衡、做足调研再行动，犹豫不决等于稳健。
old_assumption.en: Every decision deserves exhaustive analysis before acting; hesitating feels cautious and safe.

new_shift.zh: 在试错成本极低的今天，把大量“可逆小决定（Two-Way Door）”当成“不可逆大赌注”反复内耗，才是最大的隐形时间黑洞；可逆的事先跑起来再改。
new_shift.en: Over-analyzing easily reversible 'two-way door' decisions wastes massive momentum—act fast on reversible bets and reserve deep scrutiny for true one-way doors.

zh: 列出我本周正在纠结的 3 件事：[填入 3 件事]。帮我判断哪些属于“低成本可逆实验”，哪些属于“高代价不可逆决策”，并给每件可逆的事定一个 24 小时内的最小行动。
针对我担心的这个风险：[描述你的顾虑]，如果最坏情况真的发生了，修复或回滚它的实际成本到底有多大？
en: Take these 3 things I'm hesitating on: [List 3 Items]. Classify which are reversible two-way doors vs. costly one-way doors, and give a 24-hour action for the reversible ones.
For this downside risk I'm worried about—[Describe Risk]—what would it actually take to reverse or recover if it happens?

note.zh: 区分可逆与不可逆决策，是提高个人与团队推进速度的关键心智模型
note.en: Distinguishing reversible experiments from irreversible commitments keeps velocity high without recklessness

title.zh: 用“缩短反馈回路”替代单纯“拉长努力时长”
title.en: Shortening Feedback Loops Instead of Extending Effort Hours

old_assumption.zh: 一件事没起色，是因为投入的时间还不够长、还不够拼。
old_assumption.en: When progress feels slow, the fix is simply putting in more hours and grinding harder.

new_shift.zh: 反馈回路太长（比如做几个月才看到一次真实用户/结果反馈）会导致盲目偏航；把验证周期缩短到几天甚至几小时，学习速度会快好几倍。
new_shift.en: Long feedback loops cause months of blind drift—shrinking validation cycles from months to days or hours accelerates real learning far more than extra hours.

zh: 我正在推进的这件事：[描述你的目标或项目]，目前要等很久才能看到真实结果反馈。请帮我设计 3 个“把反馈回路缩短到 48 小时内”的微型验证方法。
审视我目前的 [学习/创作/做项目] 习惯，找出哪个环节的反馈延迟最高，并给出一个立刻能落地的观测指标。
en: I'm working on [Goal/Project], where real feedback currently takes too long. Design 3 ways to shrink the feedback loop to under 48 hours.
Audit my current [Learning/Building/Writing] loop—where is the slowest feedback delay, and what immediate signal can I track sooner?

signals.name: Thinking in Systems — Feedback Loops (Donella Meadows)

note.zh: 系统论核心洞察：反馈延迟与结构往往决定了系统的动态表现
note.en: Systems thinking insight: feedback delays and structure drive real-world outcomes

title.zh: 多问一层“然后呢？”，盯紧规则变化后的二阶效应
title.en: Tracing Second-Order Effects After Incentives or Tools Shift

old_assumption.zh: 看到一个新工具或新规则，只看它直接带来的眼前好处就下结论。
old_assumption.en: Judging a new tool or policy only by its immediate, first-order benefit.

new_shift.zh: 当所有人都能用同一个新手段时，激励结构和竞争生态会发生二阶变化——原本的优势可能变成新拥堵，真正的机会往往藏在下一层反应里。
new_shift.en: Once everyone adopts the same shortcut, incentives and congestion shift in second-order ways—real advantage often sits one step past the obvious effect.

zh: 针对 [某个正在普及的新工具/新规则/新趋势，如 AI 生成内容/自动化工具/某平台机制]，请帮我推演它的“一阶直接好处”以及 3 个可能出现的“二阶副作用或新机会”。
如果 [某个你打算采取的行动/习惯改变] 持续执行半年，除了预期结果之外，它可能会悄悄改变我的哪些作息、精力或人际节奏？
en: For [New Tool, Rule, or Trend], map its immediate first-order benefit plus 3 likely second-order side effects or downstream opportunities.
If I keep up [Planned Action or Habit Change] for 6 months, what second-order shifts might it trigger in my schedule, energy, or priorities?

note.zh: 二阶思维：大多数人只看第一步，看清第二步与第三步的人往往更有胜算
note.en: Second-order thinking looks past immediate effects to spot downstream reactions most people miss

title.zh: 用“最小可验证问题”给热门概念挤泡沫
title.en: Deflating Hype with One Falsifiable Question

old_assumption.zh: 某个概念被吹得很热，要么盲目追捧怕错过，要么一棍子打死觉得全是炒作。
old_assumption.en: When a buzzword is everywhere, people either jump in out of FOMO or dismiss the whole thing as hype.

new_shift.zh: 真正的区分不在“信不信”，而在“具体卡在哪”——用 1～2 个直击成本、延迟、数据或真实留存的问题，就能快速剥出真价值与真局限。
new_shift.en: Real clarity comes not from hype or cynicism, but from asking sharp questions about cost, latency, failure modes, and real retention.

zh: 最近很火的一个概念/工具是：[填入概念或工具名]。请帮我拆解：它吹嘘的理想场景是什么、目前最真实的落地卡点是什么、以及哪些场景其实用传统简单方案就够了？
给我设计一份“3 问挤泡沫清单”，以后我看到任何新名词或新方案，都能在 5 分钟内判断它值不值得我花时间深入。
en: A trending concept or tool right now is [Concept/Tool]. Break down its ideal pitch, real-world bottlenecks today, and where a simpler existing approach is already enough.
Create a 3-question hype filter I can run in 5 minutes whenever I encounter a shiny new buzzword or framework.

note.zh: 把宏大叙事拉回工程成本、维护负担与真实业务指标，是挤泡沫最有效的尺子
note.en: Checking real costs, maintenance burden, and actual metrics cuts through buzzwords fast

title.zh: 先把“默认假设”列出来，再决定要不要打破它
title.en: Listing Hidden Assumptions Before Deciding Which Ones to Challenge

old_assumption.zh: 很多前提条件是“天经地义”的，不用专门拿出来检视。
old_assumption.en: Many background premises are obvious facts of life and don't need explicit inspection.

new_shift.zh: 最大的认知盲区往往藏在“连自己都没意识到的默认假设”里；一旦把前提写到纸上，立刻就能看清哪些是铁律、哪些只是过时习惯。
new_shift.en: The biggest blindspots hide inside unexamined defaults—writing assumptions down separates real constraints from outdated habits.

zh: 针对我目前正在做的这件事：[描述你的计划或现状]，帮我列出它背后依赖的 6 条“默认假设”，并标出哪些最可能已经不再成立。
用“如果反过来会怎样”的思维，帮我挑战 [某个你一直深信不疑的行业/个人规则]，看看打破后会发生什么。
en: For my current plan or situation—[Describe Plan/Situation]—list 6 hidden assumptions it relies on and flag which ones may no longer hold.
Challenge [Rule or Convention You Take for Granted] by asking what changes if we invert it or remove the constraint.

note.zh: 剥离层层叠加的约定俗成、回到基本事实重新推理，是打破定式的核心动作
note.en: Stripping conventions back to core truths is the heart of first-principles reasoning

title.zh: 定好“何时停手”的规则，别在边际收益归零处死磕
title.en: Setting Stopping Rules Before Diminishing Returns Drain You

old_assumption.zh: 一件事没做完、没调到完美就不该停，越往后改越精细总是好的。
old_assumption.en: Keep pushing and polishing until every detail feels finished—more effort always improves the result.

new_shift.zh: 很多工作和研究在 80% 处就已经够用，后面 20% 往往边际收益极低却耗掉 80% 精力；提前设好“时间盒 / 止损线”，把省下的精力留给下一局。
new_shift.en: Past a clear threshold, extra polishing yields tiny gains at huge energy cost—clear timeboxes and stopping rules protect energy for higher-leverage bets.

zh: 我经常在 [某类任务，如查资料/改稿/调参数/挑方案] 上陷进去停不下来。请帮我设计一套“提前设定的停手规则（Stopping Rule）”，帮我及时收尾。
针对我本周的一件重要事项：[描述事项]，帮我定义“什么叫已经足够好（Good Enough to Ship）”的务实标准。
en: I tend to over-iterate and lose track of time on [Task Type, e.g., research/editing/tweaking/choosing]. Design practical stopping rules so I wrap up cleanly.
For [Important Task This Week], define a pragmatic 'good enough to ship' bar so I don't over-polish past diminishing returns.

signals.name: Algorithms to Live By — Stopping Rules

note.zh: 何时停止搜索与打磨，是日常决策中极实用却常被忽略的策略问题
note.en: Knowing when to stop searching or tweaking is a practical decision rule in everyday work

title.zh: 先看“基准率（Base Rate）”，再看吸睛的极端个案
title.en: Checking Base Rates Before Being Swayed by Outliers

old_assumption.zh: 看到一个人靠某个捷径或风口一夜翻身，就以为这件事对大多数人也是常态。
old_assumption.en: Seeing a dramatic outlier success makes it feel like a typical outcome anyone can replicate easily.

new_shift.zh: 幸存者偏差会放大极端个案；先看大样本下的真实概率、时间和投入成本，再决定要不要押注，心态会清醒很多。
new_shift.en: Outlier stories distort expectations—checking realistic base rates, timelines, and effort first keeps plans grounded without killing ambition.

zh: 我最近对 [某个方向/路径/副业/赛道] 很心动，但只看到了一些成功案例。请帮我客观分析它的“真实基准率”、常见卡点以及通常需要多久才能看到起色。
在评估 [某个目标或计划] 的时间与精力投入时，如何避免只按最顺利的“理想剧本”算账？
en: I'm drawn to [Path, Side Bet, or Goal] after seeing standout stories. Give a realistic look at base rates, common bottlenecks, and typical timelines to traction.
How can I avoid planning around a 'best-case script' when estimating time and effort for [Goal or Project]?

note.zh: 参考类预测用同类历史经验校准乐观偏差，让计划更贴近现实
note.en: Reference-class forecasting calibrates optimism bias using comparable real-world outcomes

title.zh: 把“客观事实”和“脑补故事”分开写，卡壳瞬间解开
title.en: Separating Hard Facts from the Stories Your Brain Invents

old_assumption.zh: 遇到挫折、误会或卡壳时，脑子里的猜测和情绪往往被当成了既成事实。
old_assumption.en: When things go sideways or stall, anxious interpretations and worst-case guesses feel like objective facts.

new_shift.zh: 把事件拆成两栏——“纯客观发生的事” vs “我自己推演/脑补的故事”——很多内耗和误判会当场缩小一半。
new_shift.en: Splitting a situation into 'verifiable facts' vs. 'stories and assumptions I'm adding' cuts through emotional fog and reveals what can actually be tested.

zh: 我现在因为 [某件事/某段沟通/某个进度卡点] 觉得有点堵或烦躁：[简述情况]。请帮我把“客观事实”和“我的主观猜测/担心”拆开列出来，并给出下一步最务实的验证动作。
针对 [某个让你纠结的判断]，哪些是已经有证据支撑的，哪些只是惯性联想？
en: I feel stuck or tense about [Situation, Message, or Bottleneck]: [Brief Context]. Separate verifiable facts from my assumptions/worries, and suggest one practical next check.
For [Judgment I'm Mulling Over], which parts have concrete evidence vs. habit-driven assumptions?

note.zh: 觉察自己从事实跳到结论的推理阶梯，是减少误解与情绪内耗的实用工具
note.en: Noticing how fast we jump from raw facts to interpretations reduces friction and overthinking

title.zh: 先找到“真正的唯一瓶颈”，别在非瓶颈环节拼命卷
title.en: Finding the Real Bottleneck Before Optimizing Everything Else

old_assumption.zh: 每个环节都一起优化、一起加把劲，整体效率就会跟着全面提升。
old_assumption.en: Improving every step or working harder across the board lifts overall throughput evenly.

new_shift.zh: 整条链路的上限往往卡在最窄的那一环；在瓶颈没解开前，给其他环节加再多马力也只是堆积半成品或浪费精力。
new_shift.en: A pipeline's output is capped by its tightest constraint—pushing non-bottleneck steps before clearing the real bottleneck creates pileups and wasted effort.

zh: 我推进 [某个项目/工作流/学习或创作目标] 时感觉整体卡住了：[简述各环节现状]。请帮我诊断：目前真正的“最窄瓶颈”卡在哪一步？优先该先动哪一刀？
在 [你的日常工作流] 中，哪些看起来很忙但其实不在主瓶颈上的动作，可以先放一放？
en: Progress on [Project, Workflow, or Goal] feels stuck: [Describe Steps & Current State]. Help me pinpoint the tightest bottleneck and the single highest-leverage fix.
In [Your Workflow], which busy-looking tasks sit off the main bottleneck and can wait until the core constraint is resolved?

note.zh: 约束理论：集中精力突破系统中的关键限制，往往比均匀用力更有效
note.en: Focusing improvement effort on the system's key constraint beats spreading effort evenly

title.zh: 只看“接下来投入什么、换来什么”，别被过去的沉没成本绑架
title.en: Deciding From Future Trade-Offs Instead of Past Sunk Costs

old_assumption.zh: 已经花了好几个月、好几千块或很多心血了，现在停下来或改方向就等于全盘亏光。
old_assumption.en: Having already sunk months, money, or effort into something means stopping or pivoting wastes everything you put in.

new_shift.zh: 过去花掉的时间和钱已经回不来了，继续硬撑只会多搭进未来的时间与机会；换个视角问自己：“如果今天才刚知道这件事，我还愿意从头选它吗？”
new_shift.en: Past costs are already gone—clinging to them taxes your future time and options. Ask: knowing what I know today, would I choose to start this fresh?

zh: 我目前在 [某个项目/方向/订阅或投入] 上已经花了较多时间或精力，但隐约觉得不对劲：[简述情况]。请帮我抽离沉没成本，客观评估“继续推进 vs 调整/停手”的未来得失。
帮我写 3 个犀利的问题，以后当我因为“舍不得前面投入”而犹豫是否转向时，能帮我冷静看清真实处境。
en: I've already put significant time or effort into [Project, Path, or Commitment], but it feels off: [Brief Context]. Evaluate continuing vs. pivoting based purely on future costs and upside.
Give me 3 clear questions to cut through sunk-cost attachment when deciding whether to keep going or change course.

note.zh: 识别沉没成本偏误，能帮助人在方向不对时更早释放注意力与时间
note.en: Spotting sunk-cost bias frees time and attention earlier when a path stops paying off

title.zh: 刻意找“能推翻自己看法的证据”，而不只搜集赞同理由
title.en: Actively Looking for Disconfirming Evidence Over Echoes

old_assumption.zh: 看准了一件事后，找更多支持自己的案例和观点，心里就更有底了。
old_assumption.en: Once you lean toward an idea or judgment, gathering supporting examples confirms you're on track.

new_shift.zh: 确认偏误会让人只看到想看的东西；主动问“什么情况下我的判断会错、有哪些反例”，才能在押注前看清盲区。
new_shift.en: Confirmation bias filters out warning signs—asking what would prove you wrong and seeking counter-examples exposes blindspots before you overcommit.

zh: 我目前倾向于认为：[填入你的看法或计划]。请帮我列出 4 个可能推翻或削弱这个看法的反例、潜在风险或反面视角。
如果我要验证 [某个重要假设] 到底靠不靠谱，最值得优先去查的 2 个反面证据是什么？
en: I currently lean toward [Your View or Plan]. Give me 4 counter-examples, risks, or alternative angles that could challenge or falsify it.
To test whether [Key Assumption] holds up in reality, what 2 disconfirming checks should I run first?

note.zh: 主动寻找反证是校准判断、避免陷入自我印证闭环的关键心智习惯
note.en: Seeking disconfirming evidence helps calibrate judgment before conviction outruns reality

title.zh: 信息永远不可能 100% 齐备，在“够用信息”下做决定
title.en: Deciding With 'Good Enough' Information Instead of Waiting for 100% Certainty

old_assumption.zh: 等把所有资料都看完、所有变量都算准了，再做决定才算负责任。
old_assumption.en: Wait until every fact is gathered and every uncertainty is resolved before making a call.

new_shift.zh: 现实中绝大多数决定都要在信息不完全时做出；等太久往往错过窗口或白耗精力，看清关键变量与底线后果后果断拍板更务实。
new_shift.en: Most real decisions happen under incomplete info—waiting for 100% certainty often costs time and options, whereas acting on key trade-offs and downside limits keeps moving.

zh: 我在 [某个决定/选择] 上一直等“再多看点资料再定”：[简述纠结点]。请帮我列出做这个决定真正关键的 3 个变量，以及我现在其实已经足够判断的依据。
针对 [当前纠结的选择]，帮我对比“现在就定并边走边调”与“再等两周调研”各自的机会成本。
en: I keep holding off on [Decision or Choice] to gather more info: [Brief Context]. Identify the 3 variables that actually matter and what I already know enough to judge.
Compare deciding now and adjusting as we go vs. waiting two more weeks to research [Decision]—what is the real trade-off?

note.zh: 聚焦关键变量与可承受代价，能帮助人在不完美信息下保持行动力
note.en: Focusing on decisive variables and tolerable downside keeps action moving when info is incomplete

title.zh: 揪出你从未签字、却一直在履行的“隐性合约”
title.en: Surfacing Implicit Contracts You Never Signed Yet Keep Honoring

old_assumption.zh: 很多做事规矩和人生步骤既然大家都在照做，说明那是客观条件或默认必选项。
old_assumption.en: When everyone follows a norm or milestone sequence, it feels like an objective constraint rather than a choice.

new_shift.zh: 许多卡点来自你顺手接受的“未签字合约”（比如做工具必须通用、产出必须公开发布、遇到问题先找现成方案）；一旦挑明，很多束缚当场失效。
new_shift.en: Much friction comes from unsigned contracts you treat as binding—naming them lets you renegotiate or drop rules that never served your real goal.

zh: 审视我目前正在推进的 [项目/工作流/生活安排]：[简述现状]。帮我列出 4 条我可能“默认签了字、但其实根本没必要遵守”的隐性合约，并指出哪一条最值得立刻打破。
针对 [某个让你觉得被绑住或有负担的规矩或惯例]，帮我拆解：这是真实硬约束，还是只是习惯成自然的隐性预设？
en: Audit my current [Project, Workflow, or Routine]: [Brief Context]. Surface 4 implicit 'contracts' I may be honoring by default without ever agreeing to them, and flag the easiest one to break.
For [Rule or Habit That Feels Restrictive], separate real external constraints from unexamined habits we can rewrite.

note.zh: 把看似既定的前提拆开检视，往往能发现根本不存在的隐形围栏
note.en: Inspecting taken-for-granted premises reveals invisible fences you never had to stay inside

title.zh: 别在“算错坐标系的题”上算得更准，先换题目坐标系
title.en: Stop Computing Faster Inside the Wrong Problem Coordinate System

old_assumption.zh: 推进不顺或结果不理想时，说明方法还不够细、执行还不够到位。
old_assumption.en: When a plan stalls or misses, the fix is sharper execution or more detail inside the same framing.

new_shift.zh: 有时问题卡住不是算力不够，而是“题目本身问在错误的坐标系里”（比如用线性时间去解非线性跃迁，或用局部指标代替真实结果）；换坐标系比加倍努力更有效。
new_shift.en: Stalling often means you're optimizing inside the wrong frame—shifting the problem's coordinates or unit of measure unlocks leverage that extra effort cannot.

zh: 我最近在 [某个目标/项目/难题] 上花了不少力气但进展有限：[简述现状]。请帮我跳出当前解法，提出 2 个完全不同的“问题坐标系”来重新定义这件事。
检查我目前用来衡量 [某件事进展] 的指标：[填当前指标]，它有没有可能把人引向错误方向？建议一个更贴近本质的替代视角。
en: I've put real effort into [Goal, Project, or Problem] with limited traction: [Brief Context]. Step outside current fixes and propose 2 different coordinate frames to re-pose the problem.
Check the metric I use for [Project or Habit]—[Current Metric]—and tell me how it could distort behavior or miss what actually matters.

note.zh: 切换观察问题的坐标系，常能把死结变成顺手可解的题
note.en: Changing the coordinate frame often turns a stubborn dead-end into a clean question
